title: “A Man and a Woman” by Eddie Barclay/Franck Pourcel
text: Édouard Ruault, better known as Eddie Barclay, was a French record producer. Singers under him included Jacques Brel, Dalida and Charles Aznavour.
listen: A Man and a Woman Eddie Barclay/Franck Pourcel

title: “Funeral del labrador” by Bárbara & Dick /Rosalía /Odete Lara
text: Bárbara y Dick aka Barbara & Dick were a male and female vocal duo who had a number of hits in Argentina during the 1960s and 1970s.
listen: Funeral del labrador Bárbara & Dick /Rosalía /Odete Lara

title: “La banda” by Chico Buarque/Juan Ramón/Los Garotos Las 4 Voces/Nara Leão/Tropical Combo
text: Francisco Buarque de Hollanda, popularly known as Chico Buarque (Brazilian Portuguese pronunciation: ), is a Brazilian singer-songwriter, guitarist, composer, playwright, writer, and poet. He is best known for his music, which often includes social, economic, and cultural reflections on Brazil.
listen: La banda Chico Buarque/Juan Ramón/Los Garotos Las 4 Voces/Nara Leão/Tropical Combo

title: “La felicidad” by Palito Ortega
text: Ramón Bautista Ortega is an Argentine singer and actor, better known as Palito Ortega (pronounced ). Ortega is an icon of Argentine popular music, and is considered one of the main representatives of the musical style called New wave that marked the Hispanic-American music between the years '60 and '70.

title: “Reach Out I'll Be There” by The Four Tops/Rita Pavone/Giles Pellegrin
text: "Reach Out I'll Be There"") is a song recorded by the American vocal quartet the Four Tops. Written and produced by Motown's main production team, Holland–Dozier–Holland, it is one of the most notable Motown hits of the 1960s.
listen: Reach Out I'll Be There The Four Tops/Rita Pavone/Giles Pellegrin

title: “Ciao amore, ciao” by Luigi Tenco/Dalida/Vittorio Paltrneri/ Juan Ramón/Gianfranco Pagliaro/Gabriella Marchi
text: "Ciao amore, ciao" is a 1967 song written by Italian singer-songwriter Luigi Tenco, first performed at the Sanremo Music Festival 1967, in two separate renditions, by Tenco and Italian-French singer Dalida. The song is best remembered for being Tenco's last performance before his apparent suicide on 27 January 1967, upon its elimination from the contest.
listen: Ciao amore, ciao Luigi Tenco/Dalida/Vittorio Paltrneri/ Juan Ramón/Gianfranco Pagliaro/Gabriella Marchi

title: “A namoradinha de um amigo meu” by Roberto Carlos
text: Roberto Carlos da Silva Rocha, often recognized as Roberto Carlos (Brazilian Portuguese: ) and sometimes RC3, is a Brazilian former professional footballer. He has been described as the "most offensive-minded left-back in the history of the game", and one of the greatest full-backs in history.
listen: A namoradinha de um amigo meu Roberto Carlos

title: “Hablemos del amor” by Raphael/Siro San Román
text: Spain was represented at the Eurovision Song Contest 1967 with the song "Hablemos del amor", written by Manuel Alejandro, and performed by Raphael. The Spanish participating broadcaster, Televisión Española, internally selected its entry for the contest.
wiki: Spain in the Eurovision Song Contest 1967
listen: Hablemos del amor Raphael/Siro San Román

title: “Puppet on a String” by Sandie Shaw/Al Hirt/Caravelli/Bingo Reyna/ Violeta Rivas/Las 4 Voces/Susanita Ramos
text: "Puppet on a String" is a song recorded by the English singer Sandie Shaw, written by Bill Martin and Phil Coulter. It represented the United Kingdom in the Eurovision Song Contest 1967, held in Vienna, winning the contest, becoming the first of the United Kingdom's five Eurovision wins.
wiki: Puppet on a String (Sandie Shaw song)
listen: Puppet on a String Sandie Shaw/Al Hirt/Caravelli/Bingo Reyna/ Violeta Rivas/Las 4 Voces/Susanita Ramos

title: “All You Need Is Love” by The Beatles
text: "All You Need Is Love" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles that was released as a non-album single in July 1967, with "Baby, You're a Rich Man" as its B-side. It was written by John Lennon and credited to the Lennon–McCartney partnership.
listen: All You Need Is Love The Beatles

title: “La cárcel de Sing Sing” by José Feliciano/Pepito Pérez
text: José Montserrate Feliciano García is a Puerto Rican musician. He recorded many international hits, including his rendition of the Doors' "Light My Fire" and his self-penned Christmas song "Feliz Navidad".
listen: La cárcel de Sing Sing José Feliciano/Pepito Pérez

title: “The World We Knew (Over and Over)” by Frank Sinatra/Paul Jordan/Nueva Generación
text: "The World We Knew" is a song recorded by Frank Sinatra in 1967. It is based on a composition by Bert Kaempfert, a German musician and composer.
wiki: The World We Knew (Over and Over)
listen: The World We Knew (Over and Over) Frank Sinatra/Paul Jordan/Nueva Generación

title: Vietnam War: United States Marine Corps and Army of the Republic of Vietnam troops launch Operation Deckhouse Five in the Mekong Delta.
text: The Vietnam War was an armed conflict in Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia fought between North Vietnam (Democratic Republic of Vietnam) and South Vietnam (Republic of Vietnam) and their allies. North Vietnam was supported by the Soviet Union and China, while South Vietnam was supported by the United States and other anti-communist nations.

title: Vietnam War: Operation Cedar Falls starts, in an attempt to eliminate the Iron Triangle.
text: Operation Cedar Falls was a military operation of the Vietnam War conducted primarily by US forces that took place from 8 to 26 January 1967. The aim of the massive search-and-destroy operation was to eradicate the Iron Triangle, an area northwest of Saigon that had become a major stronghold of the Viet Cong.

title: A military coup occurs in Togo under the leadership of Étienne Eyadema.
text: A coup d'état, or simply a coup, is typically an illegal and overt attempt by a military organization or other government elites to unseat an incumbent person or leadership. A self-coup is said to take place when a leader, having come to power through legal means, tries to stay in power through illegal means.

title: Louis Leakey announces the discovery of pre-human fossils in Kenya; he names the species Kenyapithecus africanus.
text: Louis Seymour Bazett Leakey was a Kenyan-British palaeoanthropologist and archaeologist whose work was important in demonstrating that humans evolved in Africa, particularly through discoveries made at Olduvai Gorge with his wife, fellow palaeoanthropologist Mary Leakey. Having established a programme of palaeoanthropological inquiry in eastern Africa, he also motivated many future generations to continue this sch…

title: In Munich, the trial begins of Wilhelm Harster, accused of the murder of 82,856 Jews (including Anne Frank) when he led German security police during the German occupation of the Netherlands. He is eventually sentenced to 15 years in…
text: Wilhelm Harster was a German lawyer, police official and convicted war criminal. An SS-Gruppenführer in the Schutzstaffel (SS), he commanded German security police and intelligence services in Kraków, the Netherlands and northern Italy during the Second World War.

title: Milton Keynes in England is founded as a new town by Order in Council, with a planning brief to become a city of 250,000 people. Its initial designated area encloses three existing towns and twenty one villages. The area to be developed is…
text: The new towns in the United Kingdom were planned under the powers of the New Towns Act 1946 (9 & 10 Geo. 6.
wiki: New towns in the United Kingdom

title: South Vietnamese junta leader and Prime Minister Nguyen Cao Ky forces his rival, Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Nguyen Huu Co, into exile while overseas on a diplomatic visit.
text: Nguyễn Cao Kỳ was a South Vietnamese military officer and politician who served as the chief of the Republic of Vietnam Air Force (RVNAF) in the 1960s, before leading the nation as the prime minister of South Vietnam in a military junta from 1965 to 1967. Then, until his retirement from politics in 1971, he served as vice president to bitter rival General Nguyễn Văn Thiệu, in a nominally civilian administration.

title: The largest-ever blizzard to hit the US city of Chicago begins.
text: The Chicago blizzard of 1967 struck northeast Illinois and northwest Indiana on January 26–27, 1967, with a record-setting 23 inches snow fall in Chicago and its suburbs before the storm abated the next morning. As of 2026, it remains the greatest snowfall in one storm in Chicago history.

title: U.S. astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee are killed when fire breaks out in their Apollo spacecraft during a launch pad test.
text: Apollo 1, initially designated AS-204, was planned to be the first crewed mission of the Apollo program, the American undertaking to land the first man on the Moon. It was planned to be launched on February 21, 1967, as the first low Earth orbital test of the Apollo command and service module.

title: The United States, Soviet Union and United Kingdom sign the Outer Space Treaty (ratified by USSR May 19; comes into force October 10), prohibiting weapons of mass destruction from space.
text: A weapon of mass destruction is a biological, chemical, radiological, nuclear, or any other weapon that can kill or significantly harm many people or cause great damage to artificial structures (e.g., buildings), natural structures (e.g., mountains), or the biosphere. The scope and usage of the term has evolved and been disputed, often signifying more politically than technically.

title: West Germany and Romania establish diplomatic relations.
text: Diplomacy is the communication by representatives of state, intergovernmental, or non-governmental institutions intended to influence events in the international system. Diplomacy is the main instrument of foreign policy which represents the broader goals and strategies that guide a state's interactions with the rest of the world.

title: Ronald Ryan becomes the last man hanged in Australia, for murdering a guard while escaping from prison in December 1965.
text: Ronald Joseph Ryan was the last person to be legally executed in Australia. Ryan was found guilty of shooting and killing warder George Hodson during an escape from Pentridge Prison, Victoria, in 1965.

title: NASA launches Lunar Orbiter 3.
text: The Lunar Orbiter 3 was a spacecraft launched by NASA in 1967 as part of the Lunar Orbiter Program. It was designed primarily to photograph areas of the lunar surface for confirmation of safe landing sites for the Surveyor and Apollo missions.

title: Italy's first guided missile cruiser, the Vittorio Veneto, is launched.
text: A cruiser is a type of warship. Modern cruisers are generally the largest ships in a fleet after aircraft carriers and amphibious assault ships, and can usually perform several operational roles from search-and-destroy to ocean escort to sea denial.

title: General Anastasio Somoza Debayle becomes president of Nicaragua.
text: Anastasio "Tachito" Somoza Debayle was a Nicaraguan politician, military officer, hydraulic engineer, and dictator who served as the 53rd President of Nicaragua from 1967 to 1972 and again from 1974 until his fall in 1979. As head of the National Guard, he was de facto ruler of the country between 1967 and 1979, even during the period when he was not the de jure ruler.

title: Alexei Kosygin arrives in the UK for an 8-day visit. He meets The Queen on February 9.
text: Alexei Nikolayevich Kosygin was a Soviet statesman who served as the Chairman of the Council of Ministers from 1964 to 1980. Following Nikita Khrushchev's removal from power, he briefly led the Soviet Union as part of a triumvirate in the mid-to-late 1960s.

title: Serious bushfires in southern Tasmania claim 62 lives and destroy 2,642.7 square kilometres (653,025.4 acres) of land.
text: Bushfires in Australia are a widespread and regular occurrence that have contributed significantly to shaping the nature of the continent over millions of years. In international terminology, an Australian bushfire is a type of wildfire, while "bushfire" remains the common Australian term for an unplanned landscape fire.

title: The Twenty-fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution (presidential succession and disability) is ratified.
text: The Twenty-fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution addresses issues related to presidential succession and disability. It clarifies that the vice president becomes president if the president dies, resigns, or is removed from office by impeachment.
wiki: Twenty-fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution

title: Burgess Ice Rise, lying off the west coast of Alexander Island, Antarctica, is first mapped by the British Antarctic Survey (BAS).
text: Alexander Island, also known as Alexander I Island, Alexander I Land, Alexander Land, Alexander I Archipelago, and Zemlja Alexandra I, is the largest island of Antarctica. It lies in the Bellingshausen Sea west of Palmer Land, Antarctic Peninsula from which it is separated by Marguerite Bay and George VI Sound.

title: American researchers discover the Madrid Codices by Leonardo da Vinci in the National Library of Spain.
text: The Madrid Codices I–II (I – Ms. 8937 i II – Ms.

title: Suharto takes power from Sukarno in Indonesia (see Transition to the New Order and Supersemar).
text: Suharto was an Indonesian military general and politician who served as the second and longest-serving president of Indonesia from 1967 to 1998. Suharto was born in Kemusuk, near the city of Yogyakarta, during the Dutch colonial era.

title: Donald Sangster becomes the new prime minister of Jamaica, succeeding Alexander Bustamante.
text: Sir William Alexander Clarke Bustamante was a Jamaican politician and leader and founder of the Jamaica Labour Party, who, on Independence Day, August 6, 1962, became the first prime minister of Jamaica.

title: Astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White, and Roger B. Chaffee are killed in a fire during a plugs-out test for Apollo 1.
text: Virgil Ivan "Gus" Grissom was an American astronaut, and one of the original Mercury Seven selected by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) for Project Mercury, a program to train and launch astronauts into outer space. Grissom went on to be a Project Gemini and Apollo program astronaut for NASA. As a member of the NASA Astronaut Corps, Grissom was the second American to fly in space in 1961.

title: The United States, Soviet Union and UK sign the Outer Space Treaty.
text: The Outer Space Treaty, formally called the Treaty on Principles Governing the Activities of States in the Exploration and Use of Outer Space, including the Moon and Other Celestial Bodies, is a multilateral treaty that forms the basis of international space law. Negotiated and drafted under the auspices of the United Nations, it was opened for signature in the United States, the United Kingdom, and the Soviet Uni…

title: Surveyor 3 probe lands on the Moon.
text: Surveyor 3 is the third lander of the American uncrewed Surveyor program sent to explore the surface of the Moon in 1967 and the second to successfully land. It was the first mission to carry a surface-soil sampling-scoop.

title: Soviet cosmonaut Vladimir Komarov is killed during the landing of Soyuz 1.
text: An astronaut, meaning 'star', and ναύτης (nautes), meaning 'sailor') is a person trained, equipped, and deployed by a human spaceflight program to serve as a commander or crew member of a spacecraft. Although generally reserved for professional space travelers, the term is sometimes applied to anyone who travels into space, including scientists, politicians, journalists, and space tourists.

title: The Soviet Venera 4 probe descends through the Venusian atmosphere, which it analyzes.
text: Venera 4, also designated 4V-1 No.310, was a probe in the Soviet Venera program for the exploration of Venus. The probe comprised a lander, designed to enter the Venusian atmosphere and parachute to the surface, and a carrier/flyby spacecraft, which carried the lander to Venus and served as a communications relay for it.

title: Mariner 5 probe flies by Venus.
text: Mariner 5 was a spacecraft of the Mariner program that carried a complement of experiments to probe Venus's atmosphere by radio occultation, measure the hydrogen Lyman-alpha (hard ultraviolet) spectrum, and sample the solar particles and magnetic field fluctuations above the planet. Its goals were to measure interplanetary and Venusian magnetic fields, charged particles, plasma, radio refractivity and UV emissions…

title: Apollo program: NASA launches a Saturn V rocket carrying the unmanned Apollo 4 test spacecraft from Cape Kennedy.
text: The Saturn V is a retired American super heavy-lift launch vehicle developed by NASA under the Apollo program for human exploration of the Moon. The rocket was human-rated, had three stages, and was liquid-fueled.

title: Pulsars discovered by Jocelyn Bell Burnell working with Antony Hewish at the University of Cambridge, for which Hewish is awarded a Nobel Prize in Physics in 1974. These rapidly pulsating radio sources are explained a year later as…
text: A pulsar is a highly magnetized rotating neutron star that emits beams of electromagnetic radiation out of its magnetic poles. This radiation can be observed only when a beam of emission is pointing toward Earth (similar to the way a lighthouse can be seen only when the light is pointed in the direction of an observer), and is responsible for the pulsed appearance of emission.

title: The first publication of Mikhail Bulgakov's novel The Master and Margarita («Ма́стер и Маргари́та»), in the form left at the author's death in 1940, concludes in the magazine Moskva, although censored portions circulate only in samizdat in…
text: Mikhail Afanasyevich Bulgakov was a Russian and Soviet novelist and playwright. His novel The Master and Margarita, published posthumously, has been called one of the masterpieces of the 20th century.

title: The Barbara Gordon version of Batgirl is introduced in Detective Comics.
text: Barbara Joan Gordon is a superheroine appearing in American comic books published by DC Comics, commonly in association with the superhero Batman. The character was created by television producer William Dozier, editor Julius Schwartz, writer Gardner Fox, and artist Carmine Infantino.

title: The first performance of D. H. Lawrence's January 1913 play The Daughter-in-Law is given at the Royal Court Theatre in London.
text: David Herbert Lawrence was an English novelist, short story writer, poet, playwright, literary critic, travel writer, essayist, and painter. His modernist works reflect on modernity, social alienation and industrialisation, while championing sexuality, vitality and instinct.

title: The 18-year-old S. E. Hinton's Bildungsroman The Outsiders is published in the United States by Viking Press. She wrote it at the age of 15–16.
text: Susan Eloise Hinton is an American writer best known for her young-adult novels (YA) set in Oklahoma, especially The Outsiders (1967), which she wrote during high school. Hinton is credited with introducing the YA genre.

title: The English playwright Joe Orton (aged 34) is battered to death by his partner, Kenneth Halliwell, who commits suicide in their north London home shortly after. Orton has completed work on a film script, Up Against It, for The Beatles…
text: The Beatles were an English rock band formed in Liverpool in 1960. From 1962 until their disbandment in 1970, the band comprised John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr.

title: American writer Norman Mailer is arrested for civil disobedience during the National Mobilization Committee to End the War in Vietnam March on The Pentagon.
text: Nachem Malech Mailer, known by his pen name Norman Kingsley Mailer, was an American writer, journalist, and filmmaker. In a career spanning more than six decades, Mailer had 11 best-selling books, at least one in each of the seven decades after World War II. His novel The Naked and the Dead was published in 1948 and brought him early renown.

title: The first issue of the magazine Rolling Stone is published in San Francisco.
text: Rolling Stone is an American monthly magazine that focuses on music, politics, and popular culture. It was founded in San Francisco, California, in 1967 by Jann Wenner and the music critic Ralph J. Gleason.

title: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn's novel Cancer Ward is banned in the Soviet Union.
text: Aleksandr Isayevich Solzhenitsyn was a Soviet and Russian author and dissident who helped to raise global awareness of political repression in the Soviet Union, especially the Gulag prison system. He was awarded the 1970 Nobel Prize in Literature "for the ethical force with which he has pursued the indispensable traditions of Russian literature".

title: Dedication of Liverpool Metropolitan Cathedral in England, designed by Frederick Gibberd, with stained glass by John Piper, Patrick Reyntiens and Margaret Traherne and a bronze crucifix by Elisabeth Frink.
text: Liverpool Metropolitan Cathedral, officially known as the Metropolitan Cathedral of Christ the King and locally nicknamed "Paddy's Wigwam" or "The Mersey Funnel", is the seat of the Archbishop of Liverpool and the mother church of the Archdiocese of Liverpool in Liverpool, England. The Grade I Metropolitan Cathedral is one of Liverpool's many listed buildings.

title: Gilbert and George first meet while studying sculpture at St Martins School of Art in London.
text: Gilbert Prousch, sometimes referred to as Gilbert Proesch, and George Passmore (born 8 January 1942) are artists who work together as the collaborative art duo Gilbert & George. They are known for their formal appearance and manner in performance art, and for their brightly coloured graphic-style photo-based artworks.

title: 1967 Basel Picasso paintings purchase referendum: The people of Basel (Switzerland) vote to purchase two paintings by Picasso to retain them in the Kunstmuseum Basel.
text: Pablo Ruiz Picasso was a Spanish painter and sculptor who spent most of his adult life in France. One of the most influential artists of the 20th century, he is known for co-founding the Cubist movement, the invention of constructed sculpture, the co-invention of collage, and for the wide variety of styles that he helped develop and explore.

title: John Willett publishes Art in a City, a pioneering sociological study of art in a single city, Liverpool.
text: John William Mills Willett, MBE was a British translator and scholar, who is remembered for translating the work of Bertolt Brecht into English.

title: Foundation of the Project Arts Centre, Dublin.
text: Project Arts Centre is a multidisciplinary arts centre based in Temple Bar, Dublin, which hosts visual arts, theatre, dance, music, and performance.
